```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(tidypopgen)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Load gt

```{r}
mad_bor_g1000_sum <-
  gt_load("../data/intermediate/rbind_data/mad_bor_g1000_sum_clean.gt",
    reattach_to = "../data/intermediate/rbind_data/mad_bor_g1000_sum_clean"
  )
mad_bor_g1000_sum <- mad_bor_g1000_sum %>% group_by(population)
```

# Load fastmixture results

```{r}
qmats <-
  readRDS("../data/intermediate/fastmixture/fastmixture_m.RData")
# check order
testthat::expect_equal(qmats$id, mad_bor_g1000_sum$id)
# add grouping variable
qmats$group <- mad_bor_g1000_sum$population
```

# Add continental region

```{r}
mad_bor_g1000_sum$Region <- "Other"
mad_bor_g1000_sum[mad_bor_g1000_sum$population %in% c("Borneo", "Sumba", "Timor"), "Region"] <- "Island southeast Asia"
mad_bor_g1000_sum[mad_bor_g1000_sum$population %in% c("BEB", "PJL"), "Region"] <- "South Asia"
mad_bor_g1000_sum[mad_bor_g1000_sum$population %in% c("CHS", "KHV"), "Region"] <- "East Asia"
mad_bor_g1000_sum[mad_bor_g1000_sum$population %in% c("ESN", "GWD", "LWK", "MSL", "YRI"), "Region"] <- "Africa"
mad_bor_g1000_sum[mad_bor_g1000_sum$population %in% c("Betsimisaraka", "Merina", "Diego", "Sakalava Tsimihety", "Betsileo", "Vezo", "Mikea", "Temoro"), "Region"] <- "Madagascar"
```

```{r}
qmats$continents <- mad_bor_g1000_sum$Region
```

# New function

```{r}
assigned_african <- list()

merina_df <- data.frame(mad_bor_g1000_sum[, c(1, 2)])
# create a dataframe of only merina individuals
merina_df <- merina_df %>% filter(population == "Merina")

for (this_k in 2:max(range(unique(qmats$k)))) { # for each k
  # list within a list - so we have $K containing runs 1 2 3
  assigned_african[[as.character(this_k)]] <- list()
  for (this_rep in 1:rle(qmats$k)$lengths[1]) { # for each run
    # get the q_matrix
    k_run <- get_q_matrix(qmats, k = this_k, run = this_rep) %>% as.data.frame()
    k_run$id <- qmats$id # add id
    k_run$group <- qmats$group # add population


    ####  1. Create a factor column in the data.frame that assigns each sample
    #         as either “African” or “non-African” based on the Population
    #         column.
    k_run$region <- qmats$continents # add the continent
    k_run$region <- ifelse(k_run$region == "Africa", "African", "nonAfrican")

    #### 2. Loop through the ancestry columns by grabbing the column references
    #       as a list and do the following for each K to determine if it is an
    #       African K or a non-African K:
    k_evaluations <- list()

    q_matrix_means <- k_run %>%
      group_by(region) %>%
      summarise(across(starts_with(".Q"), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))

    # get the list of column names - each .Q value in this matrix
    cols <- names(q_matrix_means)[grepl("^\\.Q", names(q_matrix_means))]

    # Assign each column African or non-African based on the mean
    for (i in cols) {
      if (q_matrix_means[[i]][q_matrix_means$region == "African"] > q_matrix_means[[i]][q_matrix_means$region == "nonAfrican"]) {
        k_evaluations[[i]] <- "African"
      } else {
        k_evaluations[[i]] <- "nonAfrican"
      }
    }

    #### 3. Now that you’ve assigned each K column to “African” or “nonAfrican”
    #       you can make a function that takes all the K columns as inputs and
    #       returns a sum value if the column is “African”.
    sum_af <- function(k_run, k_evaluations) {
      k_run$sum_af <- 0
      for (i in names(k_evaluations)) {
        if (k_evaluations[[i]] == "African") {
          k_run$sum_af <- k_run$sum_af + k_run[[i]]
        }
      }
      return(k_run)
    }
    k_run <- sum_af(k_run, k_evaluations)

    # And here we do the same for non-African
    sum_as <- function(k_run, k_evaluations) {
      k_run$sum_as <- 0
      for (i in names(k_evaluations)) {
        if (k_evaluations[[i]] == "nonAfrican") {
          k_run$sum_as <- k_run$sum_as + k_run[[i]]
        }
      }
      return(k_run)
    }
    k_run <- sum_as(k_run, k_evaluations)

    # k_run now contains $sum_af and $sum_as - the sum of African and
    # non-African ancestry for each individual


    # create column name
    column <- paste0(paste0("k", this_k), paste0("_r", this_rep))


    #### 4. Assign African or non_African based on which sum is greater
    k_run <- k_run %>%
      mutate(
        !!column := ifelse(k_run$sum_af > k_run$sum_as, "African", "nonAfrican")
      ) %>%
      filter(group == "Merina") %>%
      select(column)

    #### 5. Bind to Merina data to return
    merina_df <- cbind(merina_df, k_run)
  }
}
```

```{r}
merina_df[20:26, ]
```

Results show better consistency, this time up to K = 7. Last time the switch
occured at K = 5.

# Get proportions for the Merina

```{r}

        k_evaluations[[i]] <- "African"
      } else {
        k_evaluations[[i]] <- "nonAfrican"
      }
    }

    #### 3. Now that you’ve assigned each K column to “African” or “nonAfrican”
    #       you can make a function that takes all the K columns as inputs and
    #       returns a sum value if the column is “African”.
    sum_af <- function(k_run, k_evaluations) {
      k_run$sum_af <- 0
      for (i in names(k_evaluations)) {
        if (k_evaluations[[i]] == "African") {
          k_run$sum_af <- k_run$sum_af + k_run[[i]]

      return(k_run)
    }
    k_run <- sum_af(k_run, k_evaluations)

    # And here we do the same for non-African
    sum_as <- function(k_run, k_evaluations) {
      k_run$sum_as <- 0
      for (i in names(k_evaluations)) {
        if (k_evaluations[[i]] == "nonAfrican") {
          k_run$sum_as <- k_run$sum_as + k_run[[i]]
        }

    # non-African ancestry for each individual


    # create column name
    column <- paste0(paste0("k", this_k), paste0("_r", this_rep))


    #### SKIP  4. Assign African or non_African based on which sum is greater

    k_run <- k_run %>%
      filter(group == "Merina") %>%
      mutate(
        !!column := sum_af
      ) %>%
      select(column)

    #### 5. Bind to Merina data to return
    merina_df_proportion <- cbind(merina_df_proportion, k_run)
  }
}
```

```{r}
merina_df_proportion[20:26, ]
```


```{r}
long <- merina_df_proportion %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(id, population),
    names_to = c("K_run"),
    values_to = "assigned"
  )


# Ensure your K_run is in the order it appears in the dataframe
long$K_run <- factor(long$K_run, levels = unique(long$K_run))

long %>% ggplot(aes(x = K_run, y = assigned, group = id, colour = id)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Ancestry assignment",
    x = "K and run",
    y = "Ancestry assignment"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5)+
  ylim(0, 1)
```

# Get proportions for the all Malagasy individuals
